descriptionChirho: The physical foot or feet of an animal or person, used across all 8 occurrences with various prepositions and suffixes but always denoting the same body part. All multilingual glosses converge on a single meaning: English 'feet/its-feet', Spanish 'pies/pie-de-ella', Hindi 'pairon/panvon' (both meaning feet), Arabic 'rijlayhi/rijlayn' (dual feet), Korean 'baldeul' (feet), Swahili 'miguu/nyayo' (feet/soles). The four clusters differ only in grammatical inflection: construct with suffixes (S134685, S134683), definite article (S134684), and bare noun (S134687).
